summary_of_bug:
When parsers apply default options from a Properties object, they ignore OptionGroup state, so property-supplied options can be added even when a mutually exclusive option from the same group was already selected on the command line. As a result, parsing args like "-a" with properties containing "b=true" incorrectly yields both "a" and "b", while unrelated groups such as "x=true" should still be applied.

The same Properties-processing path also fails to validate that a property key corresponds to a declared option. If properties contain an unknown option like "f=true" and no such option exists in Options, parse should throw UnrecognizedOptionException instead of silently accepting it.

CLI-202.label: R
CLI-202.reason: Strong direct overlap. Both issues concern how `Properties`-based default options are integrated into parsing state after normal args are processed. CLI-202 says defaults are ignored when checking required options; the current bug says defaults are ignored when checking/updating `OptionGroup` state. Same parsing phase, same data source (`Properties`), same likely mechanism: default options are added to `CommandLine` without updating parser bookkeeping (`requiredOptions`, selected group state, etc.). This is highly diagnostic for the same parser logic block handling property defaults.

CLI-201.label: P
CLI-201.reason: Also in the same subsystem and same feature path: processing default options from a `Properties` instance in `Parser.parse()`. The mechanism differs somewhat—CLI-201 is about premature termination when a property value for a no-arg option is not `"true"`, whereas the current bug is about failing to validate/update `OptionGroup` exclusivity and unrecognized property options. Still, both point to the code that iterates over properties and decides whether/how to apply them, so this gives strong regional context and moderate mechanism context.

CLI-197.label: I
CLI-197.reason: This is about documentation/semantics of `stopAtNonOption` behavior for command-line argument parsing, not about `Properties` default-option processing, `OptionGroup` state, or required-option bookkeeping. Different mechanism and little useful regional signal for localizing the current failure.
